description: Opt-in Go overlay for repositories with a go.mod. Manages the parts of a Go module graph the gomod manager ignores out of the box (indirect requirements, /vN import paths), keeps go.mod and go.sum coherent inside the branch, and makes toolchain moves legible as toolchain moves. Extend after the default org preset.

packageRules.description: Manage indirect Go modules. Renovate disables `// indirect` requirements by default, but Go's minimal version selection makes the version written in go.mod the exact source that links into the binary — an unmanaged indirect is an unpatched indirect, and neither osvVulnerabilityAlerts nor vulnerabilityAlerts fire for a dependency that was never looked up. webgrip/ploeg shipped golang.org/x/text v0.29.0 (CVE-2026-56852, High) in ploegd 0.2.0-rc.10 for exactly this reason: Trivy saw it in the image, Renovate never had it in scope.

Group golang.org/x/* regardless of direct/indirect. They cut releases in lockstep, share go.sum entries, and `go mod tidy` resolves them together — one PR per module just rebases the others for no review value.

Never batch a Go security fix behind a group. A grouped branch is only as fast as its slowest member — one red or soaking sibling holds the whole PR, which is the opposite of what a vulnerability update needs.

Label and scope Go toolchain moves so they are not mistaken for library bumps. The `go` directive stays on Renovate's default (no updates proposed): it is a minimum-compatibility floor, and raising it drops support for older toolchains — a deliberate human decision, not a dependency bump. The `toolchain` directive does get proposals, and lands as chore(go).
Treat the golang builder image the same way: a Dockerfile FROM golang:X is a toolchain move, and it is the one that decides what actually compiles the shipped binary.
